candidates.title: Turn emailed invoices into reviewable rows

demandEvidence.chore: Bookkeepers and small finance teams retype vendor invoices received by email into a spreadsheet.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Hi all, sharing a workflow I built for bookkeepers and small finance teams who still retype vendor invoices from email into a spreadsheet.

ease.reason: A beginner can test fictional invoice rows and email text; field mapping and reliable extraction remain untested.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: bookkeeping practices may pay for less retyping; this community post establishes no buyers or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype can turn supplied sample invoices into spreadsheet rows; live mail access and accuracy need testing.

autonomy.reason: Repeated extraction and row formatting could be automated, but a bookkeeper must verify amounts and approve entries.

evidence.reason: The post directly states that bookkeepers retype emailed vendor invoices into a spreadsheet, with little detail on frequency or rules.

candidates.reason: Below the 6-point threshold (mean 5.2). A synthetic-input prototype is scorable, but the single post gives limited task detail and no implementation reference supports extraction mechanics; no post proposed.

demandEvidence.chore: Translate the Architecture Decision Record into additional languages.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I welcome constructive feedback, and welcome help with the translations.

ease.reason: A beginner can translate one supplied ADR draft with a language model and compare it with the original; no translation workflow or quality controls are documented.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: software documentation teams may pay for localization help, but this single request establishes no buyer, repeat work or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can produce one draft translation from operator-supplied text and collect bilingual review; language coverage and accuracy are unverified.

autonomy.reason: A draft can be generated from supplied text, but a qualified human must check technical meaning and approve every translation; no repeat loop is shown.

evidence.reason: The author welcomes help with translations, while the excerpt gives no target language, volume, frequency or quality criteria.

candidates.reason: Below threshold (mean 4.4): the request supports one bounded draft translation, but no recurring workflow, target language, implementation evidence or paying customer is established; a human language reviewer remains essential.
